title: Server-side session revocation on sign-out and administratively for a principal
description: POST /logout invalidates the server-side session record for the presented handle and clears the cookie on the response. After sign-out, the handle cannot resurrect an authenticated request. An administrative revoke operation is exposed on the session manager surface that invalidates every unexpired session for a given principal in one call; sign-in flows that follow the revoke issue new records with fresh handles. Client-side cookie clearing alone is not the revocation mechanism.
rationale: A session that only ends when the browser forgets its cookie is a session an attacker with the cookie can still ride. Making revocation a server-side delete on a stored record is what makes 'sign me out everywhere' honest.
